html:
Hagia Sophia, "Holy Wisdom", is the great domed church in Constantinople (now Istanbul) built for the emperor Justinian between 532 and 537. When finished it had the largest interior space in the world, and for nearly a thousand years it was the largest cathedral anywhere and the heart of Orthodox Christianity.

It replaced an earlier church burned in the Nika riots of 532. Justinian chose two scholars of geometry and mechanics, Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus, as architects, and they finished in under six years. Their dome rests on four great arches, carried at the corners on curved triangles called pendentives. A ring of windows at its base makes it seem to float. The first dome fell after an earthquake in 558 and was rebuilt higher.

Its history follows the city's:

  • Seat of the Patriarch and stage for imperial ceremony in the Eastern Roman Empire.
  • Looted by the Fourth Crusade in 1204 and used as a Latin cathedral.
  • Turned into a mosque by Mehmed II after the fall of the city in 1453; minarets were added.
  • A museum from 1935, and a mosque again from 2020.

It shaped the great Ottoman mosques, whose architects worked to match its dome.
